messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for inference-service -> image `redwood/inference:rc-2026-03-15` at 5% (us-west primary).

incident-bot: ALERT: Canaries failing healthchecks (5xx spike). metric: canary_5xx_rate=27% over last 2m. paging @oncall.

alex (oncall): saw the alert. I'm looking. pinging infra.

mira: on it — checking registry and canary logs. noticed probes failing on encoder pod.

raj: grabbing logs from canary pod (inference-encoder-rc). here's recent tail:
```
E0321 12:42:05 encoder.cpp:412] shape mismatch: expected weights[7] size 1024 but found 4096
E0321 12:42:05 runtime.cpp:88] aborting: incompatible layer layout
```

mira: that shape mismatch is weird — manifests look different across our registry replicas. tag `rc-2026-03-15` points to digest sha256:a1b2 in eu-west but sha256:c3d4 in us-west.

ci-bot: CI note — retry push happened at 2026-03-15T12:40:33, pipeline re-tagged `rc-2026-03-15` after a failed push (retry logic).

sam: so mutable tag observed; sounds like a race where the tag was moved after canary image pulled in one region. we've seen this with our current re-tag policy.

alex (oncall): customers seeing 503s? ops-sre, what is scope?

ops-sre: impact: ~3% of total inference requests (hosted API) saw encoder errors, concentrated in us-west, error budget burn ~12% in last 10m. a few paying customers reported increased latency/503s for embeddings. no PII exposed.

raj: quick mitigation ideas: 1) kill-switch feature flag to disable new encoder path (fast, in-app), 2) rollback canary to stable image, 3) pin registry to immutable digest for future.

mira: I'm going to flip the feature flag for safety — feature `use_new_encoder` -> OFF. doing it now via flag service.

alex (oncall): approved. mira please post the request/response.

mira: request:
```
POST https://flags.internal.redwood/flags/use_new_encoder/toggle
{"value": false, "actor": "mira"}
```
response: `200 OK` -> flag set false across us regions (propagation ~10s).

incident-bot: NOTE: feature flag toggled off by mira; canary errors should stop if that's the root cause. monitoring for 2 minutes.

raj: flag off cut error rate in canary to ~4% within 40s — still above baseline but much improved. recommending rollback to stable image to be safe.

sam: agreed. I'll coordinate rollback. plan: scale canary down and redeploy stable image `redwood/inference@sha256:0f9e...` to canary slots, then resume gradual rollout.

alex (oncall): go ahead. annotate ticket with customer-facing impact. ops-sre please prepare short status for customers.

sam: running rollback command now:
```
# roll canary back to stable digest
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/inference-canary inference=redwood/inference@sha256:0f9e7b4d
kubectl rollout status deployment/inference-canary -w
```

sam: rollout succeeded in us-west canary (stable digest present); healthchecks green.

raj: verifying metrics. 5xx down to 0.8% in canary window. overall latency normalized.

ops-sre: customer impact snippet for status page: 
"We observed elevated 5xx errors affecting a subset of inference requests in US-West between 12:40–12:52 UTC due to a registry tag race that caused a mismatched encoder binary to be deployed to canary pods. We disabled the new encoder feature flag and rolled the canary back to the stable digest; services are healthy. We're continuing verification and will follow up with a postmortem."

alex (oncall): handing off to raj for post-incident follow-up and postmortem. we'll keep monitoring for 1h.

raj: taking postmortem ownership. immediate action items: 
- enforce CI to push immutable digests (no re-tag on retry)
- make canary image pull use digest pin by default
- update retry logic to avoid moving tags if an earlier push succeeded
- add registry-consistency check step in deploy pipeline

mira: I'll open PRs for the deploy tooling changes and coordinate with CI.

ci-bot: CI pipeline ticket created: #INFRA-8123 (ensure immutable tag policy + pipeline check).

alex (oncall): nice work. no further paging. closing this thread for now — will append postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: canary tag race -> rollback + flag-off mitigated. duration ~12 minutes.

raj: postmortem assigned, ETA draft 48h. we'll include customer impact list and remediation plan.

ops-sre: leaving a note in the status page: follow-up emails to affected customers queued.

alex (oncall): thanks team.
